newsitem.title: SYRIA: Palestinian radicals warn Netanyahu of more attacks.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian radicals warn Netanyahu of more attacks.

text.p: A radical Palestinian group said on Friday Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu should expect more attacks by Palestinians because he was rejecting peace with Arabs.

"As long as there is occupation and (Jewish) settlements over Arab lands, Netanyahu should expect Palestinians to defend themselves with all means and to launch more confrontations," Maher al-Taher, spokesman for the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP) said.
"If Netanyahu thinks that he can have peace and the land at the same time he is mistaken," he added.

Taher was reacting to the bombing of a Tel Aviv cafe on Friday that killed three people, including the suspected bomber, and wounded 43. Israeli police believe a suicide bomber had carried out the attack.

Several Damascus-based Palestinian groups, including the PFLP, which oppose the 1993 PLO peace deal with Israel called last week on Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza Strip to carry out military attacks against Israel to confront its building of a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
The building project has enraged Palestinians who regard East Jerusalem, capured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war, as the capital of a future state.
The PFLP spokesman said meetings grouping representatives of several Palestinian factions were held in the West Bank and Gaza in the past few days and that a new uprising was starting against Israel.

"The PFLP announces to the whole world that the Palestinian people will not capitulate. We will not accept to be brought to our knees...We are announcing the renewal of the uprising against Israel," Taher said.
The PFLP has in the past claimed responsibility for attacks against Israel in which many people were killed or wounded.
"We will confront the Jewish settlers and we appeal to the Arab nation to move effectively to support the Palestinian people," Taher added.
He also called on Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to pull out of peace talks with Israel and to join other Palestinians in figthing the Netanyahu government.

"Negotiations with Israel are only serving Netanyahu and therefore the only language which the Israeli government understands is the language of resistance and confrontation," the PFLP spokesman said.
A spokesman for the Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine (DFLP) said the Netanyahu government should be held responsible for the flareup of violence in Israel.

"By insisting on building settlements at Abu Ghneim in Arab East Jerusalem, Netanyahu is igniting a new wave of violence and bloodshed for which he bears full responsibility," DFLP spokesman Ali Badwan said.
A spokesman for the Fatah Uprising led by Colonel Abu Mousa called for an urgent Arab summit to discuss joint action against Netanyahu's government.

"Netanyahu is ignoring the whole world by continuing his anti-peace actions and repressive measures against Palestinians. Arabs should convene an urgent summit to discuss how to deal jointly with the aggressive policies of the Zionist enemy."
